name: Hong Kong International Airport

runway.v: three parallel runways (07L/25R, 07C/25C, 07R/25L), each 3,800 m long and 60 m wide

ppr.v: all non-commercial flights need prior approval from the Director-General of Civil Aviation, and final approval from the Aerodrome Control Supervisor on the day of flight
ppr.quote: All non-commercial fixed wing aircraft and helicopter flights at HKIA must have prior approval from the Director-General of Civil Aviation.

handling.v: flights for hire or reward are handled by the Hong Kong Business Aviation Centre, with parking on its own apron
handling.quote: Flights operated for Hire or Reward handled by Hong Kong Business Aviation Centre

noise.v: night noise-mitigation measures every day from 23:00 to 07:00 local time (preferred runway and approach use, not a ban)

slots.v: Level 3 coordinated airport: every arrival and departure needs a slot from the Hong Kong Schedule Coordination Office (part of the Civil Aviation Department); business and general aviation ad hoc requests go through its Online Coordination System; only emergency, state, military, humanitarian and technical flights are exempt
slots.quote: Since July 2008, Civil Aviation Department (CAD) has assumed the role of the Coordinator for HKIA ... Given that HKIA is a Level 3 airport ... all airlines/aircraft operators must obtain a slot from HKSCO for each aircraft movement

permits.v: private (non-revenue) flights need prior clearance, and charter flights a permit, from the Director-General of Civil Aviation; apply at least 3 working days before arrival/departure through the CAD e-filing system (at least 2 weeks for new or infrequent operators)
permits.quote: Prior clearance from the Director-General of Civil Aviation is required ... at least 3 working days before the anticipated arrival/departure date

notes: Noise window converted from UTC (1500-2300 UTC) to Hong Kong time (UTC+8); Hong Kong has no daylight saving time. The AIP page read is the 4 Sep 2025 amendment inside the eaip_20250710 package; newer packages (e.g. eaip_20260806) exist on ais.gov.hk but their AD 2 VHHH text page could not be opened from here, so re-check before publishing. The airport authority's 2021 press release confirms HKBAC operates the business aircraft facilities at HKIA (source hk-aahk-hkbac). The newest package found on ais.gov.hk is eaip_20260806, but its AD 2 VHHH text page was not found by search, so status stays partial until the current AD 2 page is read. Slots from the CAD Schedule Coordination Guidelines for HKIA, Issue 14.1 (Sep 2018), still posted by CAD; the CAD annual report 2024-25 (cad.gov.hk/reports/an2024-2025/html/en/ch9.html) confirms the Hong Kong Schedule Coordination Office of the CAD still allocates slots, and AIC 07/26 (2 Apr 2026) says all aircraft operators must obtain runway slots from HKSCO. The 2018 guidelines say night is 1400-2259 UTC (22:00-06:59 local) and night movements are limited under the Airport Authority's Noise Quota Count scheme, with a few night slots for quieter types; not recorded as a curfew because the source is from 2018.
